items.stem: Why does a rate of 48 percent, instead of a rate near 100 percent, among identical twins fit a diathesis-stress view?

options.text: Identical twins share the same genes, so the many who were not diagnosed suggest that experiences also matter
options.why: A vulnerability that is present in both twins does not always lead to the disorder without additional influences.

options.text: A diathesis-stress view says that stress alone causes the disorder in every person
options.why: The model combines vulnerability with stress and does not claim that stress alone is sufficient.

options.text: A lower rate shows that the diagnosis was made incorrectly
options.why: Nothing suggests incorrect diagnoses.

options.text: Identical twins share half of their genes, so a lower rate is expected
options.why: Identical twins share essentially all of their genes.

items.stem: A researcher wants to test whether shared home environment, rather than shared genes, explains the pattern. Which additional study would best address this?

options.text: A survey of fraternal twins about their parents' child-rearing styles
options.why: A survey of one kind of twin pair does not separate genes from environment.

options.text: An interview with clinicians about their diagnostic habits
options.why: Clinicians' habits do not separate genes from environment.

options.text: A measurement of both kinds of twins on an unrelated personality test
options.why: An unrelated test does not address the question.

options.text: A comparison of identical twins raised apart with identical twins raised together
options.why: Comparing identical twins in different environments separates genetic similarity from shared environment.
